_comment: Spanish counterpart of blocklist.json. Same rules: exact match only, and
the same deliberate refusal to strip clinical or protective vocabulary.
Spanish needs more care than English on two counts:
1. `negro` is the ordinary colour word and is ON the bundled board. It
is not blocked. Neither is `gitano`, which is an ethnonym before it
is anything else. Blocking either would break real vocabulary to
catch a use we cannot detect from a word list anyway.
2. Regional profanity differs sharply (peninsular vs. Latin American),
so the list covers both rather than assuming one variety.
Words that are profanity in one register and neutral in another (`coger`
is `to take` in Spain and vulgar in much of Latin America) are KEPT:
`coger` is on the Acciones page, and prediction that refused to complete
a board word would be a bug.

_why: AAC users experience abuse at far higher rates than the general
population, and lacking the vocabulary to describe bodies, sex, and
assault is a documented barrier to disclosure. Stripping clinical and
protective vocabulary out of prediction would make the app worse at the
moment it matters most. These words stay, and build-lexicon.mjs asserts
that no future blocklist edit removes them.
